text.overview: A sustained Grade IV+ line up the South Peak's north ridge, adjacent to the mountain's famously vertical 1,000-ft north face.

siblingTrailheads.name: Hozomeen Campground / Hozomeen Lake Trailhead (upper loop)

lastAnswer.notes: No page describes this route's approach (the AAJ north-face and Zorro pages name no trailhead). South Peak routes generally use Hozomeen Lake trailhead at Hozomeen Campground (onehikeaweek) but nothing ties this north ridge to it; Lightning Creek and Skyline II are also used on this mountain.

text.approach: From the Lightning Creek trailhead on Ross Lake, the first-ascent party hiked east past Willow Lake, then left the trail to bushwhack through timber and avalanche debris, crossed a ravine, and climbed steep dirt and brush to open timber on the broad shoulder south of the peak. They reached meadows near 5,000 ft and bypassed cliff bands to a saddle at about 6,200 ft below the buttress — roughly six hours from the trailhead — where they bivouacked.

text.overview: A serious, poorly-protected Grade IV technical rock route on the North Peak's southwest side; very few successful ascents are reported, and protection is difficult.

siblingTrailheads.name: Hozomeen Campground / Hozomeen Lake Trailhead (upper loop)

lastAnswer.notes: No page found that describes this route's approach; SummitPost and Mountaineers returned 403. Only lead is the sibling's Hozomeen Campground, unverified.

text.approach: A two-stage approach and the second stage is the part that stops people. Day one is a long haul of 11-plus miles under heavy loads from the road to a camp just north of the peak - the same Hozomeen Ridge / border-swath ground used by the north-side scrambling routes, reached from Silver-Skagit Road out of Hope, B.C. From that camp the approach to the base took the first ascent party a tedious and painstaking 4.5 hours: downclimb a loose third-class gully, which the party described as dangerous but the lesser of the two evils, then cross several precipitous rocky ribs and steep, unstable ground to traverse into the launch point below the wall. Budget the base approach as a half-day objective in its own right and do it in daylight. Confirm the NPS border-gate status before planning; the crossing at Hozomeen has been closed to vehicles and foot traffic since 2020, with no end date given on the park's fire-closure page updated 14 September 2026.

text.overview: A Grade IV, 5.9 technical rock route on the North Peak's west face, very difficult to protect and among the hardest routes on the mountain.
text.descent: From the summit, take the easy north-side ground: reverse the Northeast Buttress / North Route line, downclimbing the Class 2-3 northeast ridge, treating the short very exposed Class 4 eroded segment near 7,600 ft with maximum care, then descending the north cirque snowfields to the saddle and back to camp. lastAnswer.notes: Mountain Project (East Ridge, South Face, West Face only), Wikipedia, trailcatjim: no north route described. Standard access is the PCT north trailhead at Snoqualmie Pass, or Gold Creek to Joe Lake; neither tied to a north route. SummitPost and Mountaineers 403.

text.approach: Reached from the Tank Lakes side of the Alpine Lakes high route, via the Foss River trails, not from Chetwoot Lake.
text.descent: Reverse the ascent: down the north ridge, round the northeast nose, and across talus to the saddle below the Tank Lakes plateau.

trailhead.name: Necklace Valley Trailhead (East Fork Foss River)

identifiedBy.fact: Descent via North Ridge / Northeast Nose to Iron Cap Pass, 1 mi to Tank Lakes, then down to Necklace Valley and out to the East Fork Foss trailhead

lastAnswer.notes: Medium: the Tank Lakes side connects to Necklace Valley TH on a page (trailcatjim finished the traverse there), and route text excludes Chetwoot/West Fork Foss; but no page names a start for this exact route, and that traverse arrived from Dingford Creek. Peakbagger 403, WTA reports not opened. The placements agree within 100 m.

text.approach: From Marblemount on WA-20, drive the Cascade River Road (FR-15) about 19-21 miles (paved to roughly mile 10, then gravel/washboard) to the Eldorado trailhead (~2,150 ft). Cross the North Fork Cascade River and follow the unmaintained Eldorado climbers' trail through forest and a boulder field to treeline, then to Eldorado Basin/Roush Creek camps (~6,000-6,300 ft). Ascend the Eldorado Glacier snow dome to the ~7,500-ft notch on Eldorado's lower East Ridge, traverse ~1.5 miles north across the upper Inspiration Glacier to Klawatti Col (7,800 ft), then continue easily to the nearby Klawatti-Austera Col (7,900 ft) to start the ridge.

text.overview: A Class 3 scramble along Klawatti's north ridge from the Klawatti-Austera Col, working around a rock tower nicknamed 'The Smokestack' before finishing on the summit crest.
text.descent: Downclimb the ridge crest back around The Smokestack via its west-side gully, return to the Klawatti-Austera Col, then to Klawatti Col. From there re-cross the Inspiration Glacier to the notch on Eldorado's East Ridge, descend the Eldorado Glacier, and follow the climbers' trail to the trailhead.
